question: Which single practice most consistently reduces drug administration errors during intraoperative team communication?

answers.text: Using colour-coded syringe labels according to IS0 26825 standards

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Colour-coded labels are an important system-level safeguard but do not directly prevent errors arising from verbal orders or misheard communications.

answers.text: Closed-loop communication with read-back of drug name, dose, and route

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Closed-loop communication — where the receiver repeats the order back and the sender explicitly confirms — is the most robust individual-level intervention proven to reduce drug administration errors.

answers.text: Requiring a second anaesthetist to countersign every drug draw

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Double-checking is valuable in some contexts but is impractical during rapid intraoperative management and is not the most consistently effective single practice.

answers.text: Preparing all syringes in the pharmacy rather than at the anaesthetic machine

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pharmacy preparation reduces preparation errors but does not address communication failures during administration.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the prevention strategies block. Closed-loop communication (sender → receiver repeats back → sender confirms) is the single most impactful individual-level communication safeguard.
Correct. Closed-loop communication with read-back is the evidence-based cornerstone of preventing intraoperative communication-related drug errors.
